text: Three motor cars with blinds drawn arrived at Uckfield Police Court to-day. Several young girls, hooded, emerged and entered the Court, on the occasion of the reappearance of Hayley Morris and his newly-wedded wife before the'magistrates.

label: text
text: A pathetic figure in the witness box was the girl of fifteen who broke down at the previous hearing.

label: text
text: The witness hesitatingly described certain incidents and said Morris told her not to tell anyone and if she wanted money to write to him.

label: text
text: A girl of twenty said that when Morris asked her to go to his room she appealed to Mrs. Morris, who said: "If you like me, you will go, or he will stop my allowance."

label: text
text: Witness said she would go if Mrs. Morris would, and said Mrs. Morris was present during the alleged incident in the room.

text: Britain's could exports in 1024 were 51.2 per cent. of the world exports, compared with 49.8 in 1913.

label: text
text: Giving evidence to the Coal Commission, Sir Richard Redmayne said he could see no striking change on the world basis, detrimental to British coal interests.

label: text
text: He opined that in a quarter of a century there would be no oil in the United States, and the world supply of oil would suffice more than 80 to 100 years.

text: M. Radek, who has been elected Rector, said the work of the University would be strictly scientific, principally social and would be entirely free from propaganda.

text: Final farewell to Hongkong's departing Governor, Sir R. E. Stubbs, K.C.M.G., will be taken to-morrow between 11:15 and 11:30 a.m. at Queen's Pier where representatives of all interests in Hongkong will be present in large numbers. Both interesting and significant of the reciprocation of the feelings of goodwill animating the Hongkong Government and the community with relation to the Chinese notwithstanding the events originating in alien interference is the expressed wish of representative elders of the New Territories to be present at Queen's Pier in order that they may be their presence and good wishes bear testimony to the beneficial results attending the British administration of the New Territories in general and Sir R. E. Stubbs' personal interest and furtherance of their interests in particular. Their presence is entirely at their own request.

label: text
text: There will be five or six of these elders present at the pier to-morrow and they will be introduced to Sir R. E. Stubbs by the Hon. Mr. D. W. Tratman, Secretary for Chinese Affairs.

label: text
text: The s.s. "Kalyan" will arrive in Hongkong on Sunday morning and as nearly as can be gauged at the present time Mr. Cecil Clementi will land at Queen's pier at about 9:45. He will be met by Government officials, Unofficial members of the Legislative Council, naval and military representatives and prominent members of the community, will proceed to the Council Chamber where will be administered the oaths and the Constitution read and will then proceed to Government House accompanied by a guard of honour composed of selected men from the East Surrey Regiment. GOVERNOR'S PRIVATE SECRETARY. Mr. T. J. Gaisford-St. Lawrence, Private Secretary to H.E. the Governor, left this morning for Home via Shanghai and America by the "Empress of Canada." It is not known definitely whether Mr. Gaisford-St. Lawrence or Capt. Neville will accompany Sir. R. E. Stubbs to Jamaica.

label: text
text: Before Mr. E. W. Hamilton at the Kowloon Magistracy this morning, Li Wing-chan, of 19, Nathan Road, was charged with removing 595 lbs. of tobacco, 21,625 cigars and 218,400 cigarettes from his bonded warehouse to another part of the premises, and alternatively with keeping the tobacco in an unlicensed warehouse.

label: text
text: Mr. J. A. Fraser, assistant superintendent of Imports and Exports, prosecuted.

label: text
text: Defendant pleaded guilty to the charge of moving the tobacco, which he said was done as the tobacco was deteriorating owing to leaks in the roof.

label: text
text: Mr. Fraser said that since the defendant took the business over from Mr. Atienza two months ago, he had applied for permission to store the tobacco in a shed in the yard. The shed was divided into two by a stone wall, one part being used as a warehouse. On October 22 a revenue officer visited the premises and found that the tobacco had been transferred from the warehouse to the other part used as a bedroom.

Conditions similar to those experienced by "Fatshan" passengers on the last trip of that vessel were reported upon the return yesterday from Canton of the s.s. "Honam," those Chinese who could afford to pay the exorbitant suma demanded being able to land and those who could not have to return to Hongkong. The majority found the necessary money.
The s.s. "Fatshan" will return to Canton this afternoon.

text: By a strange circumstance a breakdown van belonging to the Kni Tack Motor Bus Company found itself in a vegetable garden in its endeavour to get to Hunghom yesterday afternoon.

label: text
text: According to the statement of the driver of the van, he turned from Sai Kung Road into Kowloon City Road when the vehicle struck the bank, overturned, and fell into the garden.

label: text
text: The occupants of the van got again before it toppled over.

label: text
text: An inspector of the same Company witnessed another accident at Tsun Wan Road, near Kau Kang village, when a motor truck belonging to the Tai Hing contractors, of Portland Street, Yaumati, struck a bank and overturned.

label: text
text: A Chinese accountant who was riding in the truck was injured and had to be taken to the Kwong Wah Hospital.

label: text
text: According to the eye-witness, the truck swerved in order to avoid a pedestrian, and in so doing steered into the bank.

label: text
text: A motor car owned by a Chinese pulled up near the Naval Yard yesterday afternoon owing to a truck being in the way. A tram car following close behind failed to observe the signal and ran into the motor car, doing some damage to the latter.

label: text
text: At Pokfulam Road, a P.W.D. lorry knocked down a seven-year-old Chinese boy, who was injured in the head and body and had to be taken to the Government Civil Hospital.

label: text
text: No untoward incidents have taken place since the opening of the postern of the Western (British) gate on Shameen and residents walk generally unmolested and almost unnoticed in the City. Their presence there occasions no comment on the part of passers by and unless they bring parcels back to Shameen they are unmolested. Strike pickets claim the right to examine parcels and to prohibit the carrying into Shameen of foodstuffs.

label: text
text: It was inevitable that in the absence of Chinese workers the sanitary arrangements of the City have had to be left to individuals themselves and conditions as regards the streets and other public places have been of necessity not of the best. Since the arrival of non-Cantonese Chinese scavengers arranged for through the Sanitary authorities at Hongkong, things in this respect have improved considerably.

text: An unemployed American seaman named Vertie Vlon Brunson was charged before Mr. S. B. B. McElderry at the Central Magistracy this morning, with unlawful possession of two automatic pistols and 52 rounds of ammunition.

label: text
text: Detective Sergeant O'Donovan said that he visited the Seamen's Institute yesterday evening on certain information received by him and arrested the defendant following the discovery of the arms in his possession.

label: text
text: His Worship told the defendant that it was a serious charge, and remanded the case for one week, bail being allowed on $2,000.

text: A depression or typhoon of unknown intensity within 120 miles of Lat. 15 N., Long 129 E., which in an earlier warning was stated to be moving W.N.W., is reported this morning to be nearly stationary in Lat. 17 N., Long 128 E. (North-East of the Philippines).

label: text

text: The executive of the German National party in a manifesto outlining its attitude towards the Locarno treaties says that the pact greatly disappointed the party because of their principles regarding war-guilt and the state of the army. Article sixteen of the League covenant had not been upheld and there had been no reduction in the occupation periods of the Rhineland and Saar as stipulated.

text: A message from Damascus states that the newspaper "Omran" says that on the 23rd inst. a communiqué from the British Consulate stated that the bombardment was expected to re-start on the 24th in a bit the Consulate would do its best to send British subjects from the danger zone.

label: text
text: Later the same night the French authorities announced that guarantees had been given for payment of the fines imposed on the city, and therefore the danger of bombardment was temporarily over.

label: text
text: The authorities have arrested Hassan el Karrath, who led the band in the insurrection and 43 other insurgents, while 160 Damascenes and suburban residents have been charged with connivance.

label: text
text: The paper adds that three were executed. "We do not know the nature of their crime."

label: text
text: Alarmed at the reports from Syria, the State Department has instructed the American Ambassadors at Paris to make representations to the French Government for the protection of American life and property at Damascus.

label: text
text: According to official reports from Damascus, while the French residents were removed to barricaded positions, the bombardment proceeded without notice to other foreigners.

label: text
text:
A demand for indemnification will undoubtedly be made to Paris in respect of damage to American property immediately the details are received.
It is not known what damage has already been done, though hitherto no American has been reported hurt.

label: text
text:
Sarrail to be Recalled.
It is reported that one of the first acts of the new Government will be to recall General Sarrail from Syria.

label: text
text: The newspapers are very anxious over the situation in Syria. "L'Echo de Paris" says that M. Doumergue has requested M. Painleve to do what is necessary to re-establish tranquility at any cost. A correspondent of the same paper accuses General Sarrail of pro-Turkish and anti-Arab leanings and of upholding Turkish Freemasonry.

label: text
text: "Figaro" and "Le Matin" criticise General Sarrail's alleged failure to supply information. The latter says that General Sarrail's reports talk about the weather and the dearness of living, with a post-script of two lines in regard to the gravest events.

label: text
text: “Le Matir” declares that General Sarrail's lack of balance is damaging the prestige of France in the world.
